html:
The Krĩcatijê, or Krikati, are a Timbira people of the cerrado savanna of southwestern Maranhão state in Brazil. They speak a language of the Jê family, close to those of the Canela and Gavião.

Timbira villages were laid out as a great circle of houses around a central plaza, linked to it by paths like the spokes of a wheel, and life was organised around ceremonies such as log races. As cattle ranchers moved into Maranhão in the 1700s and 1800s, the Krikati lost much of their land. After a long struggle their territory was legally recognised in the early 2000s, though it is still disputed by settlers. Their neighbours include the Guajajara. See Brazil.
